title: Our biggest growth bottleneck is that accountants actively advise their small-business clients against self-service tools like ours — we need a channel strategy to either partner with accountants or reach clients directly without alienating them.

record.text: Our biggest growth bottleneck is that accountants actively advise their small-business clients against self-service tools like ours — we need a channel strategy to either partner with accountants or reach clients directly without alienating them.
record.detail: A significant number of small-business owners in Serbia rely on a trusted accountant for everything, and many of those accountants tell their clients that self-service tools create errors and compliance risk. Some of that concern is genuine and some of it is about protecting a fee relationship. Either way, it means potential subscribers hear negative things about us before they ever see the product. We have tried running online ads, going to small-business trade fairs, and offering a two-month free trial, and while those tactics bring in some users, we keep hitting a ceiling. We are not sure whether the right move is to build a version of the product designed for accountants to use on behalf of multiple clients — turning them from competitors into resellers — or to find a direct channel that does not trigger their resistance. We do not have a sales team; this is partly a strategy question and partly a product and pricing design question. We want to grow from 1,400 to around 3,000 subscribers within two years without taking on investment that would change how we run the company.
